title: Perfect tensor tests of an infinitesimal proper-support inverse system
statement: Work over $\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$ with schemes [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-affine-spectrum], algebraic spaces [def-trf-algebraic-space], and the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. Fibre products are sheaf fibre products [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers]. Separated, finite type and proper morphisms use [def-sfb-space-morphism-properties]. Finite presentation means quasi-compact, quasi-separated and locally finitely presented on etale scheme charts. Use quasi-coherent modules on the small etale ringed sites [def-trf-space-quasi-coherent-module] and tensor pullback and direct image [def-trf-space-etale-module-functors]. A module is finitely presented if etale locally it has a presentation $\mathcal O^r\to\mathcal O^s\to F\to0$ with $r,s$ finite. Base-flatness means flatness of stalks on etale scheme charts over the corresponding local rings of the base [def-pc-scheme-module-flat-over]. Proper support means there exist a closed immersion $i:Z\hookrightarrow X$ with $Z$ proper over the base and a finite type quasi-coherent module $G$ on $Z$ such that $i_*G\simeq F$ [def-sfb-space-proper-quot-functor]. Let $(A_n)_{n\geq1}$ be an inverse sequence of commutative rings with surjective transition maps whose kernels are locally nilpotent, meaning every element of each kernel is nilpotent, and set $A=\varprojlim_n A_n$. Let $X\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ be separated and finitely presented, put $X_n=X\times_A\operatorname{Spec}A_n$. For every $n\geq1$ let $M_n$ be a finitely presented quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_{X_n}$-module, flat over $A_n$, with support proper over $A_n$, with specified isomorphisms $M_n\otimes_{A_n}A_{n-1}\simeq M_{n-1}$ for $n\geq2$. Use unbounded derived categories of module sheaves [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Write $D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_X)$ for the full subcategory with quasi-coherent cohomology. Regard $M_n$ as a module on $X$ by direct image along $X_n\hookrightarrow X$; the given transition isomorphisms followed by quotient maps define its inverse-system maps. The symbol $R\varprojlim_{D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}}M_n$ denotes the homotopy inverse limit in this full derived subcategory: it fits into the product triangle $K\to\prod_{n\geq1}M_n\xrightarrow{1-\mathrm{shift}}\prod_{n\geq1}M_n\to K[1]$, with products taken in $D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}$ and projections $q_n:K\to M_n$ induced by the first arrow. Here the shift has $n$th component equal to the transition map composed with the $(n+1)$st projection. Let $K$ be this homotopy inverse limit [lem-sfb-space-inverse-module-derived-limit]. For every perfect $E\in D(\mathcal O_X)$, meaning etale locally a bounded complex of direct summands of finite free structure modules [def-weil-pbc-strict-perfect-coefficient-package], the object $R\Gamma(X,K\otimes^{\mathbf L}_{\mathcal O_X}E)$ is perfect in $D(A)$ [def-pc-perfect-ring-complex]: it is isomorphic to a bounded complex of finitely generated projective $A$-modules. Derived tensor is computed with K-flat resolutions [def-pc-kflat-complex], and $R\Gamma$ is the right derived global sections functor [def-pur-ringed-site-zeroth-hypercohomology].

source.place: Tag 0CX6, lemma-compute-against-perfect, clause (1), perfectness assertion; Situation 0CX4, situation-existence.

proof.text: Put $i_n:X_n\hookrightarrow X$, $f_n:X_n\to\operatorname{Spec}A_n$, $E_n=Li_n^*E$, and $C_n=R\Gamma(X_n,M_n\otimes^{\mathbf L}E_n)$. Derived pullback preserves perfectness: on each strict-perfect chart its terms and retraction maps pull back as in [lem-weil-pbc-strict-perfect-ringed-pullback-model]. The morphisms $f_n$ are finitely presented: base-changing a finite presentation on scheme charts gives a finite presentation with the same generators and relations. Their relative diagonals are base changes of the closed diagonal of $X/A$, so they remain separated. Apply [lem-sfb-space-module-proper-carrier-support] to replace the given proper carrier by proper scheme-theoretic support. The module $M_n$ in degree zero now satisfies every coefficient hypothesis of [lem-sfb-proper-support-tensor-perfect]. Thus $Rf_{n,*}(M_n\otimes^{\mathbf L}E_n)$ is perfect and quasi-coherent. The small-etale/Zariski equivalence [lem-sfb-scheme-derived-etale-qcoh-comparison] and perfectness detection [lem-sfb-etale-detects-perfect] give a Zariski-perfect complex on $\operatorname{Spec}A_n$. By [lem-pc-perfect-affine-bounded-projective] and [lem-pc-affine-qcoh-derived-equivalence], its derived sections $C_n$ are represented by a bounded finite-projective $A_n$-complex. Derived sections of $Rf_{n,*}$ equal derived sections on $X_n$ by [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-pushforward-composition].

source.place: Tag 0CX6, finite-level perfectness; spaces-perfect.tex Tag 0A1P, lemma-base-change-tensor-perfect.

proof.text: For $n\geq2$, apply [lem-sfb-space-flat-complex-base-change] to $f_n$, $E_n$ and the degree-zero complex $M_n$, with base change $\operatorname{Spec}A_{n-1}\to\operatorname{Spec}A_n$. The qcqs hypotheses hold since $f_n$ is separated and finitely presented; the coefficient is base-flat by assumption. Since $X_n$ is quasi-compact by [lem-sfb-space-fp-qcqs-source], the perfect $E_n$ has quasi-coherent cohomology by [lem-sfb-space-perfect-uniform-tor], so $E_n\in D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_{X_n})$ as that statement requires. Its ordinary pullback is $M_{n-1}$ by the specified transition isomorphism. Pullback composition identifies the perfect factor with $E_{n-1}$. Hence the base-change morphism identifies the derived pullback of $Rf_{n,*}(E_n\otimes^{\mathbf L}M_n)$ with $Rf_{n-1,*}(E_{n-1}\otimes^{\mathbf L}M_{n-1})$. Under [lem-sfb-scheme-derived-etale-qcoh-comparison], the affine tensor formula [lem-pc-affine-derived-pullback-tensor-tilde] and the quasi-inverse [lem-pc-affine-qcoh-derived-equivalence] identify this with $C_n\otimes^{\mathbf L}_{A_n}A_{n-1}\xrightarrow{\sim}C_{n-1}$. These are the scalar-extension adjuncts of the maps induced by the actual transition $M_n\to M_{n-1}$: the exchange map in the cited base-change statement is defined by that pullback counit, followed by the specified coefficient quotient. No flatness of $X_n/A_n$ or of $A_{n-1}$ over $A_n$ is used. The composition comparisons used here respect units and counits by [lem-sfb-space-derived-etale-chart-calculus].

source.place: Tag 0CX6, compatibility under base change; spaces-perfect.tex Tag 0A1P and its base-change input.

proof.text: Let $F_n=i_{n,*}M_n$ in degree zero. A closed immersion is affine, so [lem-sfb-space-affine-module-higher-image-vanishing] gives $Ri_{n,*}M_n\simeq F_n$. The space $X$ is quasi-compact by [lem-sfb-space-fp-qcqs-source], so $E\in D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_X)$ by [lem-sfb-space-perfect-uniform-tor]; $i_n$ is affine, hence quasi-compact and separated. By [lem-sfb-space-qcqs-derived-projection-formula], $F_n\otimes^{\mathbf L}E\simeq Ri_{n,*}(M_n\otimes^{\mathbf L}E_n)$. Apply derived sections and [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-pushforward-composition] to obtain $T_E(F_n)\simeq C_n$ as objects of $D(A)$, with $C_n$ restricted from $A_n$. These identifications commute with the transition maps: $i_{n-1}=i_n\circ(X_{n-1}\hookrightarrow X_n)$, and both sides apply derived sections to the coefficient quotient $M_n\to M_n\otimes_{A_n}A_{n-1}\simeq M_{n-1}$ and the identity on $E$; the projection morphism is explicitly the counit-mate in the cited statement. Thus this is an isomorphism of towers, not just separate isomorphisms of objects. The composition comparisons used here respect units and counits by [lem-sfb-space-derived-etale-chart-calculus].

source.place: Tag 0CX6, identification of X and X_n tests; spaces-perfect.tex Tag 08IN, lemma-cohomology-base-change.

proof.text: By [lem-sfb-space-fp-qcqs-source], $X$ is qcqs, since its base is affine. The given $K$ is the homotopy inverse limit of the tower $F_n$ in $D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}$ by [lem-sfb-space-inverse-module-derived-limit]. Apply [lem-sfb-space-perfect-tensor-test-holim] to this tower and $E$. It gives $R\Gamma(X,K\otimes^{\mathbf L}E)\simeq R\varprojlim_n T_E(F_n)$. The tower identifications of Step 3 identify the latter with $R\varprojlim_n C_n$ in $D(A)$. In particular, this argument never replaces a product in $D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}$ by an ambient product.

source.place: Tag 0CX6, preservation of derived limits by the perfect test functor.

proof.text: Every $C_n$ is perfect by Step 1 and the reduction adjuncts are isomorphisms by Step 2. The ring maps are surjective with locally nilpotent kernels exactly as required by [lem-sfb-perfect-inverse-ring-reconstruction]. Therefore $R\varprojlim_nC_n$ is perfect over $A$. Transport its bounded finite-projective representative through the derived isomorphism of Step 4. This proves that $R\Gamma(X,K\otimes^{\mathbf L}E)$ is perfect for the arbitrary perfect $E$ originally chosen.
